subject: Evaluating per-seat vs throughput bundles for pilot
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@clinicai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Holt <megan.holt@clinicai.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing: per-seat vs throughput

Hi Naomi / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — ClinicAI is excited about the latency and cost gains Redwood showed. We're getting the procurement team involved to scope a 3-month paid pilot. A few quick facts about our expected usage to help you recommend a packaging approach:

- Team: 6 product/infra engineers will be hitting the API during business hours; 2 ML engineers will run nightly batch embedding jobs.
- Traffic: daytime QPS is spiky (bursts up to 30 qps for short periods), average steady-state token consumption ~200k tokens/day, nightly embedding run ~2M tokens.
- Requirements: low-latency for interactive product (<=150ms P95) and data isolation (VPC).

Our procurement asks: which pilot bundle gives us predictable cost while letting us avoid heavy overprovisioning? Specifically: per-seat (seat includes some request units) vs throughput-based (token buckets / throughput capacity) — which is a better fit for a mixed interactive + batch workload? Also, any short-term credits or pilot pricing terms you can offer would help get approval.

Can you propose 1–2 practical options and an example quote? We'd like to close pilot terms this week.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform
ClinicAI


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@clinicai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Megan Holt <megan.holt@clinicai.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing: per-seat vs throughput

Hi Sanjay — great question, and thanks for the usage notes. High-level recommendation first, then two concrete options:

High-level: For a mixed interactive + batch profile like yours, we usually recommend a hybrid pilot: a small dedicated throughput bucket for predictable background embedding jobs (to avoid contention), and a per-seat or low-latency endpoint allocation for the interactive product. That reduces tail latency risk during bursts while keeping unit economics efficient for batch.

Option A — Seat-focused pilot (simpler operationally)
- 6 seats (entitles each seat to interactive endpoints with fair-share CPU/GPU capacity)
- Shared throughput pool for embedding (metered tokens, monthly cap)
- Pros: simple billing per-seat, clear team ownership; fast to enable.
- Cons: may need temporary throttling during big bursts unless we size seats conservatively.

Option B — Hybrid throughput pilot (better for bursty + heavy batch)
- Small dedicated throughput bucket (equivalent to steady 10 qps sustained with burst capacity to 35 qps) for interactive endpoints (keeps P95 low)
- Separate nightly batch job bucket (pre-reserved tokens to run embeddings)
- Pros: predictable cost for batch; lower P95 latency.
- Cons: slightly more configuration; procurement prefers a single invoice often.

Attached: Pilot_Options_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with line-item examples) and a short T&Cs summary.

Pilot pricing guidance (rough):
- Option A: $6k/mo for seats + $1.2k/mo embedding token bucket (pilot discount applied)
- Option B: $8k/mo for combined throughput buckets (includes burst buffer)

Ben and Priyom are looped in for final pricing and any seat-credit options — Ben will suggest a compact quote we can present to procurement. If you can confirm which option you prefer and whether a single invoice vs separated line-items matters for your finance team, we can get a formal quote and PO-ready doc over today.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Account Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Pilot_Options_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), T&Cs.pdf (summary)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing: per-seat vs throughput (internal)

Naomi / Priyom — quick internal note on recommended pricing construct:

- Given ClinicAI's burst profile, I prefer Option B but with simplified invoicing: we create a combined pilot SKU that maps to a single invoice line but behind the scenes allocates token pools for interactive vs batch. That avoids procurement pushback on multiple lines and keeps SRE happy.
- Offer a 20% pilot discount for months 1–3 and include one-time onboarding credit ($1,500) to cover VPC setup and testing.
- Quote should show sample monthly consumption and a conservative bump (30%) above their stated average to cover initial burst underestimation.

I'll draft a single-line quote and attach a short justification to help procurement.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@clinicai.com>, Megan Holt <megan.holt@clinicai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing: per-seat vs throughput — ClinicAI pilot quote attached

Hi Sanjay / Megan — thanks for the details; we've consolidated internally and attached an updated pilot quote (ClinicAI_Pilot_Quote_v2.pdf). TL;DR recommendation: go with the hybrid combined-pilot SKU (Option B) — it gives you predictable batch capacity for nightly embeddings and a burst-friendly allocation for interactive endpoints while keeping procurement happy with a single invoice line.

Key items in the attached quote:
- 3-month pilot: combined pilot SKU with reserved throughput, burst buffer, and a separated nightly batch allocation
- Pilot price: $7,200/mo (after 20% pilot discount) + one-time onboarding credit applied ($1,500)
- SLOs: P95 <= 150ms for interactive endpoints during the pilot (regional: us-west), VPC onboarding estimated 5 business days after PO
- Next steps: 1) confirm you want to proceed with the combined SKU, 2) send PO to procurement@redwood.com, 3) we'll issue SOW and start onboarding.

If finance needs the invoice broken into two lines we can do that, but it will increase the visible monthly amount (we'll include an explanation for procurement). Please confirm and I can generate a DocuSign SOW.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Account Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ClinicAI_Pilot_Quote_v2.pdf
